messages:
maria: Noticed a synchronized flutter of 150-250ms write latency on local NVMe across a small cohort in ap-southeast1 and us-west1 starting ~0300 UTC. GPU attach jitter spiked at same time. Short log sample below.

maria: ```
[gnode-az2] write_ms_series=12,180,14,220,9,198,11
attach_failures: +2.7% windowed
```

boysun: hmm. that pattern looks like a convoy of smallwrites lining up. any cron jobs around :00/:30?

maria: janitor runs at :00/:30 in those pools. also scheduler metadata syncs at :02/:32 for a subset. overlap window suspicious.

anu: do we have SMART/errors? temp spikes?

maria: SMART clean, temps steady. NVMe vendor firmware had recent update last month but we didn't flip any power-state knobs.

devops-bot: Metric anomaly: nvme.write.p95 > 120ms on 5 hosts in ap-southeast1 (detected 1745561100). Creating alert ticket IT-4123.

boysun: can you run a micro-fio on one of the affected hosts? 4k randwrite, iodepth 8.

maria: running now: `fio --name=rwtest --rw=randwrite --bs=4k --iodepth=8 --runtime=300 --group_reporting`

maria: result: observed periodic amplitude pulses matching the janitor cadence. when i paused janitor on that host, pulses disappear.

anu: interesting. pausing globally isn't great. what's the cost impact of slowing janitor down?

maria: estimate: prolonging cleanup by ~2.5x on these pools. backlog grows, some ephemerals might stick around longer, but immediate GPU attach reliability improves.

boysun: short mitigation: decrease janitor concurrency to 25% on the two affected pools for 4 hours and add a routing preference to avoid hosts with recent janitor runs (<8m). I'll run the rollout.

ops-bot: Rolling out: `opsctl rollout --service janitor --pool pool-ephemeral-asia --concurrency 25%` (change id: rc-9882). Stagger 8s per node.

maria: after ~5mins latency settled to ~30-40ms spikes and attach failures returned to baseline. Looks correlated.

anu: long term fixes: 1) janitor write coalescing / batching small writes 2) run janitor with an ioclass niced to avoid hitting NVMe scheduler 3) stagger janitor start times per rack.

boysun: also vendor suggested disabling aggressive PM state transition in firmware (ticket VT-9867). vendor claims it reduces tail latency for sustained smallwrite bursts but requires reboot and EOL impact unknown.

maria: schedule firmware toggle only on a canary host during off-peak. if good, consider wider rollout in maintenance window.

ops-bot: Created follow-up task: ENGINFRA-2215 (janitor ioclass and coalescing work).

maria: I'll open a PR to add a soft pref in routing: prefer hosts where last_janitor_ts > 480s for attach decisions. small change, low-risk.

boysun: noted. tara (cost), can you run a 7d estimate on extra storage + egress if janitor remains slow for sustained week?

anu: putting a note: avoid fleet-wide reboot for vendor toggle until we have canary data.

maria: tl;dr: mitigated by throttling janitor concurrency + routing preference. experiments and vendor canary planned. will update IT-4123 and ENGINFRA-2215. :white_check_mark:
